project.name: curl
project.commit_note: The staged vulnerable workspace reproduces the crash in the vendored `curl_fuzzer` harness under `_work/src/curl_fuzzer`. The saved `patch.diff` only removes unrelated `conncache.h` includes from `lib/easy.c`, `lib/http.c`, and `lib/http2.c`, so patch-grounded corroboration is unavailable for this crash site.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42502820 (curl): Index-out-of-bounds found by fuzz target curl_fuzzer_http [ubsan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42502820
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `runtime error: index 11 out of bounds for type 'FUZZ_RESPONSE [11]'` in `fuzz_send_next_response()` at `curl_fuzzer/curl_fuzzer.cc:440`. The staged 348-byte TLV witness populates primary mock-server response slots 1 through 10; slot 1 is a 124-byte `HTTP/0.0 302` reply and slots 2 through 10 are zero-length TLVs whose `.data` fields are still non-NULL because `fuzz_parse_tlv()` stores `tlv->value` even when `tlv->length == 0`. `fuzz_handle_transfer()` seeds `response_index` at 1, and when `fuzz_open_socket()` later tests `responses[1].data` it skips the immediate-shutdown branch for the primary socket. On the crashing `fuzz_send_next_response()` invocation, the function still reads the last in-bounds slot 10 and then increments to index 11. The shutdown test uses `sman->response_index > TLV_MAX_NUM_RESPONSES` instead of `>=`, so once `response_index` becomes 11 the left bound check is false and the right operand reads `sman->responses[11].data` one element past the `FUZZ_RESPONSE[11]` array. The staged `patch.diff` is unrelated to this crash site.

evidence_note: Stage 02 used the staged `sample_info.json`, `patch.diff`, `sanitizer_trace.txt`, `default_crash_trace.txt`, `reproduction_report.json`, the saved `poc`, the reviewer `trace_feedback.json`, and the staged vulnerable sources under `_work/src`. A static TLV decode of `poc` was taken with the checked-in helper `curl_fuzzer/read_corpus.py`; no compilation, rerun, or instrumentation beyond Stage 01 artifacts was performed. `trace_feedback.json` required removing an unsupported URL/FOLLOWLOCATION causal step, and `run_flags.json` set `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so no runtime disambiguation path was used.

source.description: First project-code parse of the attacker-controlled TLV corpus. These decoded type, length, and value fields drive the response-table state that later reaches the off-by-one shutdown check.
source.value_from: A static decode of the staged 348-byte `poc` (SHA-256 `9103fd2037be598c37e75e67ba9dc9ee85608f0248104ccedd2239f6dd2b9847`) yields the crash-relevant TLVs: `type=17` primary-socket RESPONSE1 with length 124 carrying the `HTTP/0.0 302` reply, `type=18..26` primary-socket RESPONSE2..10 each with length 0, and `type=32` secondary-socket RESPONSE1 with length 42. Only the primary response table receives enough populated slots to reach index 11.
source.note: The TLV parser first materializes each attacker-controlled header and payload pointer here; later switch cases use those decoded fields to populate `responses[]`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The primary response-table state that reaches the crash is created here. On the witness, `responses[1]` becomes the 124-byte redirect reply and `responses[2..10]` become zero-length but non-NULL entries because the macro stores `tlv->value` regardless of `tlv->length`.

root_cause.description: The shutdown guard is off by one. After incrementing `response_index`, it rejects only values greater than 11, not equal to 11, so the right-hand operand dereferences `responses[11]` even though `responses` is declared with 11 elements indexed `0..10`.
root_cause.note: The staged `patch.diff` does not touch this crash site, so no saved patch corroborates the missing `>=` bound check.

sink.description: UBSan crash site. When `response_index` has just been incremented to 11, this condition reads one element past the `FUZZ_RESPONSE[11]` array.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `runtime error: index 11 out of bounds for type 'FUZZ_RESPONSE [11]'` at this exact expression.

parser_admitted.description: After TLV parsing and option setup, the staged witness enters the transfer loop. The saved stack confirms the reproduced path is `fuzz_handle_transfer -> fuzz_send_next_response`, and the static TLV decode shows only primary socket manager 0 has enough populated response slots to reach index 11. The same witness also contains URL and nonzero FOLLOWLOCATION TLVs, but this pass does not score a finer redirect-path subtrace because the saved artifacts do not establish that libcurl-internal control edge directly.

fine_trace.note: Source. The TLV decoder first materializes attacker-controlled type, length, and payload-pointer state here. For the staged witness, the crash-relevant iterations decode primary RESPONSE1, primary zero-length RESPONSE2..10, and a single secondary RESPONSE1.

The witness stages primary response slots 1 through 10 here. Slot 1 receives the 124-byte `HTTP/0.0 302` reply. Slots 2 through 10 are present as zero-length TLVs, and the macro still stores each `tlv->value` into `.data`, so those entries are non-NULL even though `data_len == 0`. By contrast, the witness gives socket manager 1 only a single `SECOND_RESPONSE1`, so only primary socket manager 0 can ever reach index 11.

Before any socket traffic is processed, `fuzz_handle_transfer()` seeds each socket manager with `response_index = 1`. The crashing path therefore counts later response sends starting from slot 1 rather than slot 0.

The witness has no primary RESPONSE0 TLV, so `fuzz_open_socket()` sends no immediate data on connect. But because step 2 made `responses[1].data` non-NULL, this immediate-shutdown branch is not taken and the primary socket stays `FUZZ_SOCK_OPEN` for later `fuzz_send_next_response()` calls.

On the crashing invocation, the current index is 10. That follows from step 3's `response_index = 1` initialization plus the saved UBSan fact that the later line-440 check runs with index 11 after the post-send increment. Because step 2 left primary slots 2 through 10 non-NULL and step 4 kept the socket open, this call still fetches the last in-bounds primary entry `responses[10]`.

Root cause. After step 5 uses slot 10, the increment makes `sman->response_index == 11`. `FUZZ_SOCKET_MANAGER` declares `FUZZ_RESPONSE responses[TLV_MAX_NUM_RESPONSES]` and `TLV_MAX_NUM_RESPONSES == 11`, so the only valid indices are 0 through 10. The left side of the guard is still false because it uses `>` rather than `>=`, so the bound check does not stop at the array limit.

Sink. Because step 6 left `sman->response_index == 11` and the array has only slots 0 through 10, this right-hand operand probes `responses[11].data` one element past the declared `FUZZ_RESPONSE[11]` array. The saved UBSan trace reports `index 11 out of bounds for type 'FUZZ_RESPONSE [11]'` at this exact expression.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42502820 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/curl_fuzzer_http` and reproduced `runtime error: index 11 out of bounds for type 'FUZZ_RESPONSE [11]'` in `fuzz_send_next_response` with stack `fuzz_send_next_response -> fuzz_handle_transfer -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

format.name: curl_fuzzer HTTP TLV corpus
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 348-byte witness in `poc` with SHA-256 `9103fd2037be598c37e75e67ba9dc9ee85608f0248104ccedd2239f6dd2b9847`. A static TLV decode yields 26 TLVs total. The witness includes one primary RESPONSE1 TLV of length 124 carrying the `HTTP/0.0 302` reply, primary RESPONSE2 through RESPONSE10 TLVs each of length 0, one URL TLV of length 22 containing only `0x20` bytes, one FOLLOWLOCATION TLV of length 4 with bytes `20 20 20 20`, and one secondary-socket RESPONSE1 TLV of length 42. In the staged vulnerable `curl_fuzzer`, even zero-length response TLVs set non-NULL `responses[i].data` pointers, so the primary response table remains populated through slot 10. Combined with `response_index` starting at 1, the exact witness drives the primary mock server to the final in-bounds slot and then makes the post-increment shutdown test probe `responses[11].data`, reproducing the saved UBSan crash. The artifacts do not justify a broader trigger contract beyond this exact TLV corpus witness.
